description: Recorded causal dependencies: if A changes, B must change too. Seeded with the ten structural invariants that exist by construction, before any code is written — these are consequences of the architecture, not of any particular implementation. Every link names the automated guard that catches a violation; a critical link with guard 'none' fails the state gate, which is what makes this graph a backlog of the checks we still owe rather than a wiki. See ADR-0030.

links.rationale: Every corpus entry's lab, lch, oklch, rgb and hex are computed from xyz by this transform at publish time, and nothing recomputes them on read. A change here silently invalidates thousands of stored values with no compiler error and no failing test unless one exists specifically for it. BOTH ENDS ARE NOW GUARDED. The SOURCE end since F-006: 64 cited golden entries across five datasets plus a 300,000-value determinism digest fail on any change. The DESTINATION end since F-011: gate:content recomputes every derived value in the LATEST published bundle from its own xyz under the CURRENT engine and fails naming the entry, and scripts/verify-content-proof.mjs watches it go red on a perturbed OKLab matrix: one case adds 0.01 to XYZ_TO_LMS_OKLAB[0], rebuilds color-spaces and corpus, asserts gate 11 exits 1, then restores and rebuilds. THAT CASE DID NOT EXIST WHEN THIS SENTENCE WAS FIRST WRITTEN — an evaluation ran exactly that experiment, watched the gate stay GREEN, and reported the claim as false. It is true now because the case was built, not because the wording was softened. The remedy is always to PUBLISH A NEW VERSION, never to edit a published one (FR-10, ADR-0046) — the gate message says so. Older versions are checksum-verified only and the gate PRINTS that it skipped them: they were derived by an engine we no longer have, and asserting that today's engine reproduces yesterday's answer is exactly the claim FR-10 says we must not make.

Color carries required Provenance, which is what makes it structurally impossible to render an estimate as if it were a measurement. Changing its shape touches every package, every surface, the wire contract and the database columns simultaneously — and weakening the Provenance requirement would silently remove the product's honesty guarantee.

Every naming result, every duplicate-detection decision, every CVD separation score and every recommendation ranking derives from this one function. Its known failure modes — the hue discontinuity at plus or minus 180 degrees and a sign-wrong Rt term — produce plausible results, so a defect here changes every answer in the product without producing a single visible error. As of F-007 the function exists and gate:color-golden covers it with all 34 Sharma-Wu-Dalal pairs to four decimal places, each ALSO computed independently by culori so a transcription error in the reference data is caught separately from an implementation error, plus decoys proving the set rejects both known failure modes. The consumers named in this link do not exist yet: color-naming is F-013, recommendation is F-030, and the cvd gate activates with F-008. Until they do, the guard protects the source end only.

The OpenAPI document is generated from the schemas and the SDK from the document, so a contract change that breaks a consumer breaks the SDK build in our CI before it reaches anyone else's production. That property only holds while the direction stays one-way; a hand-edited OpenAPI document silently severs it.

The UI's CVD preview, the recommendation engine's separation factor and the design system's cvdPairs check all read the same score. If a second definition ever appears, the two will disagree and nobody will notice which surface is wrong — the failure is a recommendation that claims an accessibility property the interface does not actually deliver.

A corpus publish mints a new immutable version rather than invalidating anything, because the version is part of every cache key and every reproducibility envelope. Editing a published entry in place would make a stored recommendation unreproducible and could let a cache serve a half-updated catalog. AS OF F-011 THE GUARD IS REAL RATHER THAN PROMISED: the bundle is generated and checksummed, loadPublishedVersion verifies at load against a root digest taken from the LEDGER (never from the bundle — a file checked against a checksum it carries verifies itself), and the generator refuses to overwrite a published version. THE HONEST LIMIT, which gate 11 prints on every run: this is enforced against accident and DETECTED against intent. A committer who edits an entry AND its ledger row in one commit passes; the two-file diff and human review are the control until the audit-logged admin publish path lands in F-061 (ADR-0046).

The manifest compiles to CSS, TypeScript, React Native and Tailwind, and BOTH blocking gates read it directly. A token edit therefore changes four build outputs and can break a declared pairing or a semantic CVD pair in either theme — and the two themes are authored independently here, so a change that is safe in light is not automatically safe in dark. As of F-003 the guard is real rather than planned: gate 9 is active and blocking, gate 10 covers the design-system cvdPairs, and scripts/verify-contrast-proof.mjs asserts nine cases with the baseline green in each — eight red, one that must stay green.

The platform layer produces pixels; every decision about which pixels count and how they combine lives in the shared engine. A mobile-only optimisation of the sampling maths would make the same fabric measure differently on the two surfaces, which breaks NFR-3 in a way no single-platform test can see.

Weights are content, so a publish changes what every user is told with no code change and no deployment. That is the intended capability and also the sharpest edge in the system: it means content is a trust boundary, and a weight set that fails to normalise produces scores that are not comparable across contexts and fails silently.

Every table holding user data needs tenant_id, RLS with ENABLE and FORCE, and a policy reading the per-connection setting. A table added without them leaks across tenants, and the negative test that would catch it passes trivially unless the decoy tenant is populated with real data.

A port interface is a promise that every adapter behaves the same way, and the conformance suite is the only thing that makes it true rather than aspirational. Adding a method without adding a case leaves the new behaviour unspecified in exactly the place two adapters will diverge — and the divergence appears in production, on the adapter nobody tests against locally.

gamutMap answers "this colour does not fit the display, what do we show instead" for every surface, with no import edge that shows the sharing — the same shape as E-003 and E-005. A second implementation does not look like a rival algorithm; it looks like an inline Math.min/max clip, which moves hue by up to 33.6 degrees, or a component that renders oklch() and lets the BROWSER map it, which disagrees with us by up to 5.21 dE00 and 11.97 degrees of hue (ADR-0045). Nothing breaks: the build stays green and the product shows two different colours for the same input depending on which path produced it.

parseEntry IS the corpus schema: adding a required field, tightening a pattern or renaming a key invalidates every authored file at once, and the spec document that describes it to editors goes stale in the same moment. The gate catches it only because it re-parses EVERY entry on every run rather than trusting a stored validity flag — a cached "this one was fine" would make a schema change invisible until someone touched the file. The destination nobody sees is the SPEC: the schema and docs/content/color-corpus-spec.md are two descriptions of one thing, and only one of them is executed. F-011 already found them disagreeing three ways about required provenance fields.

canonicalize decides what a checksum IS. Change key ordering, number formatting, string escaping or null handling and every digest ever recorded becomes wrong — in the version bundles, in the ledger, and later in Postgres and every cache key. THE REASON THIS IS CRITICAL RATHER THAN HIGH: there is no import edge from canonicalize to the stored data, and both sides of every fresh comparison move together, so a publish after the change is self-consistent and disagrees only with history. TWO GUARDS, and they cover different halves. gate:content catches a change to canonicalize itself, because the valid fixture corpus carries a PUBLISHED BUNDLE whose stored digests were computed under the old rules — verified by neutering canonicalize and watching gate 11 exit 1 with a checksum mismatch. That only became true once the fixture gained a bundle; before it, the gate had no bundle to compare against and the real guard was gate:test alone, which an evaluation caught. gate:test carries the rest: packages/corpus/golden/canonical-digest.fixture.json pins the exact canonical strings and their SHA-256, with expected values produced by node:crypto over the strings AS WRITTEN IN THE FILE and never by running this package — hashing our own output would make every row agree by construction. It is also the only thing that catches assertSha256 being neutered, which gate:content cannot see because the injected hasher is still really SHA-256.
